title: For a sheaf the map to the plus construction is an isomorphism
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, and let $\theta:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G^+$ be the canonical map to its plus construction [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction]. Then $\theta_U:\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal G^+(U)$ is bijective for every object $U$, i.e. $\theta$ is an isomorphism of presheaves; in particular $\mathcal G^+$ is a sheaf.

source.place: Sites, Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus), part (3) (item-plus-iso, tag 00WE), with its proof

mathlib_searches.query: if P is a sheaf then the canonical map P to P plus is an isomorphism
mathlib_searches.verdict: generalization in another formalism: isIso_toPlus_of_isSheaf (Plus.lean:256, verified with sed -n 250,270p) for `plusObj` over a Grothendieck topology; Mathlib's plus construction `plusObj` is defined for a Grothendieck topology (colimit over covering sieves `J.Cover X`), not for a site given by covering families as in Stacks 00VH [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with the plus construction of [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction]; the identification of the two plus constructions is itself a theorem (cofinality of the sieves generated by covering families, Stacks Sites Sections 00ZB/00ZG), so this is not a one-line specialization
